core_obligations: The direct image is a sheaf (proof lines 8220-8221): the sheaf condition for the direct image of a constant set is exactly assumptions (1) and (2) together with the definition of the functor.
Adjointness (proof lines 8221-8223): the second assertion is the restriction to sheaves of the adjointness between the direct image and the stalk functor.

Stalks of a presheaf and of its sheafification (proof lines 8224-8231): for any set the author computes the maps out of the stalk of a presheaf into it by a chain of adjunctions and identifies them with the maps out of the stalk of its sheafification, whence the equality of the two stalks.
proof_roadmap: Check the sheaf condition for the direct image of a constant set using the two covering assumptions.
Restrict the known adjointness to sheaves.
Compare the stalks of a presheaf and of its sheafification through adjunctions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a set-valued functor whose values satisfy two covering conditions gives a sheaf-valued direct image, an adjunction with the stalk functor, and the equality between the stalks of a presheaf and of its sheafification (statement lines 8199-8217). The proof is short but complete: the first assertion follows from the definition of a sheaf together with the two assumptions (proof lines 8220-8221); the second restricts the known adjointness to sheaves (proof lines 8221-8223); and the third follows from a chain of adjunction identifications comparing the maps out of the two stalks (proof lines 8224-8231). The non-formal content is the comparison of the stalks through adjunctions. The claim is H1: three short verifications, each written out.
